questions.question: Chaoite, Buckminsterfullerene and Graphene are related to which element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaoite, Buckminsterfullerene, and Graphene** are all allotropes of **Carbon**.
 
• Carbon is known for its ability to form various allotropes due to its versatility in bonding.
 
• These allotropes have unique structures and properties:
 
 
• **Chaoite:** A relatively rare allotrope of carbon, which is believed to be formed under extreme conditions such as those found in meteorite impacts.
 
• **Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀):** A spherical molecule also known as a "buckyball", consisting of 60 carbon atoms arranged in a structure similar to a soccer ball.
 
• **Graphene:** A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice, known for its remarkable strength and electrical conductivity.
 
 
 
• These materials have significant applications in various fields such as electronics, materials science, and nanotechnology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon** is a non-metal element with the atomic number 6 and is the fourth most abundant element in the universe by mass.
 
• It is the basis of organic chemistry, as it forms the backbone of organic molecules found in all living organisms.
 
• Carbon's ability to form stable bonds with many elements, including itself, allows for the vast diversity of organic compounds.
 
• Allotropes of carbon like diamond and graphite have been known for centuries, while newer allotropes like graphene and fullerenes have been discovered in recent decades, leading to advancements in technology and materials science.

questions.question: The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**gross domestic product**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as the **gross domestic product (GDP)**.
 
• GDP is a primary indicator used to gauge the health of a country's economy.
 
• It represents the total dollar value of all goods and services produced over a specific time period.
 
• GDP can be calculated using three approaches: the production (or output) approach, the income approach, and the expenditure approach.
 
• It includes all private and public consumption, government outlays, investments, and exports minus imports that occur within a defined territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** includes GDP plus any income earned by residents from overseas investments, minus income earned within the domestic economy by foreign residents.
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is GNP minus depreciation (a measure of the wear and tear on the country's capital goods).
 
• **Net Domestic Product (NDP)** is GDP minus depreciation.
 
• GDP is often adjusted for inflation to reflect real GDP, which provides a more accurate depiction of an economy's size and how it's growing over time.

questions.question: The technique of classical dancing was codified by ______ in about the 5th century B.C.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The technique of classical dancing was codified by **Bharata** in about the 5th century B.C.
 
• Bharata is traditionally credited with authoring the **Natyashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music.
 
• The **Natyashastra** is a comprehensive text that outlines the rules and principles for classical dance forms and has been influential in shaping Indian classical dance traditions.
 
• It covers various aspects of stagecraft, including makeup, costumes, acting, and directing, making it a seminal work in the field of performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharata Muni** is believed to have lived during the period between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• The **Natyashastra** is written in Sanskrit and consists of 36 chapters with a total of 6,000 verses.
 
• The treatise provides detailed guidelines for actors, dancers, and musicians, ensuring the preservation and propagation of classical arts.
 
• Classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and others have drawn heavily from the principles laid out in the **Natyashastra**.
 
• The work has played a crucial role in the cultural and artistic history of India, influencing not just dance but also other forms of art and literature.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1929**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Child Marriage Restraint Act** was passed in the year **1929**.
 
• This act is also known as the **Sarda Act**, named after Harbilas Sarda, who introduced it.
 
• The act aimed to restrain the practice of child marriage in India by setting the minimum age of marriage to 18 for males and 14 for females.
 
• It was a significant step towards improving the social condition of women and children in India.
 
• The act has been amended several times, with the most recent amendments raising the minimum age of marriage to 21 for males and 18 for females.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Child Marriage Restraint Act** was a pioneering law for its time, addressing a deeply rooted social issue.
 
• Despite the enactment of the law, child marriage continues to be a challenge in many parts of India, necessitating ongoing efforts and enforcement.
 
• The act was one of the early legal reforms in India aimed at improving the status of women and children.
 
• Subsequent laws like the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 have further strengthened the legal framework against child marriage in India.

questions.question: What is the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Ghats**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Western Ghats** are the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India.
 
• These mountain ranges run parallel to the western coast and act as a barrier to the moisture-laden winds coming from the Arabian Sea.
 
• As these winds ascend the Western Ghats, they cool down, condense, and result in heavy rainfall on the windward side of the mountains.
 
• This phenomenon is known as orographic rainfall and is crucial for the monsoon season in the western coastal regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• They play a significant role in influencing the climate of the region by intercepting the monsoon winds.
 
• The Western Ghats extend from the state of Gujarat in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, covering a distance of about 1,600 km.
 
• They are also home to numerous endemic species of flora and fauna, contributing to their ecological importance.

questions.question: Which condition causes bone pain, poor growth, and soft, weak bones that can lead to bone deformities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rickets**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets** is a condition that causes bone pain, poor growth, and soft, weak bones that can lead to bone deformities.
 
• It is most commonly seen in children and is often caused by a deficiency of vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate.
 
• Symptoms of rickets include delayed growth, pain in the spine, pelvis, and legs, and muscle weakness.
 
• Rickets can be prevented by ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D and calcium through diet and exposure to sunlight.
 
• Treatment typically involves dietary supplements and addressing any underlying conditions that may contribute to the deficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cerebral Palsy** is a group of disorders that affect a person's ability to move and maintain balance and posture.
 
• **Pertussis**, also known as whooping cough, is a highly contagious respiratory disease caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis.
 
• **Asplenia** refers to the absence of a spleen or its function, which can increase the risk of infections.
 
• Ensuring a balanced diet rich in essential nutrients and regular check-ups with a healthcare provider can help prevent and manage conditions like rickets.
 
• Education on the importance of vitamin D and calcium, as well as safe sun exposure practices, is crucial for preventing rickets.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of microfinance institutions in India?

options.text: Increased reliance on informal lending sources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enhanced financial inclusion**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Enhanced financial inclusion** is a significant advantage of microfinance institutions in India.
 
• Microfinance institutions provide **financial services to low-income individuals** who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• These institutions play a crucial role in **empowering women** by providing them with the necessary financial resources to start and expand their businesses.
 
• Microfinance helps in **poverty alleviation** by offering credit to the underserved sections of society, enabling them to improve their economic conditions.
 
• They also promote the development of **small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)**, which are essential for economic growth.

• These institutions operate in both rural and urban areas, providing a range of financial products such as **microloans, savings accounts, insurance, and remittance services**.
 
• MFIs have been instrumental in **reducing the reliance on informal lending sources**, which often charge exorbitant interest rates.
 
• The growth of microfinance in India has led to **increased financial literacy** and awareness among the economically weaker sections of society.
 
• Despite challenges, the microfinance sector continues to expand, contributing significantly to the **financial inclusion agenda** of the country.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is the maximum extent of alluvial soil found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has the maximum extent of alluvial soil in India.
 
• Alluvial soils are widespread in the northern plains and the river valleys of India.
 
• These soils are formed by the deposition of sediments brought down by rivers.
 
• Uttar Pradesh, being part of the Indo-Gangetic plain, is predominantly covered with alluvial soil.
 
• This type of soil is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture, supporting the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alluvial soils are classified into two types: Bhangar (old alluvial soil) and Khadar (new alluvial soil).
 
• Bhangar soils are found on higher lands and are less fertile, while Khadar soils are found in the floodplains and are more fertile.
 
• The Indo-Gangetic plain, covering states like Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, and West Bengal, is also rich in alluvial soil.
 
• Alluvial soil is characterized by its light texture, good porosity, and high water retention capacity, making it ideal for intensive agriculture.
